CEO Commentary
“We delivered strong third quarter results. Record net revenue of $8.0 billion drove diluted earnings per share of $1.34, up 10% year-over-year, a return on tangible common equity of 18.5%, and an efficiency ratio of 55.9%. The net charge-off ratio improved to 51 basis points. Our exceptional business mix and increasingly strong operating discipline helped us deliver high returns, productivity, and prudent risk management while strengthening revenue growth. We reported a full quarter of BTIG results, which drove an increase of 69.3% year-over-year in capital markets revenue. Our Payments transformation gained momentum and delivered combined revenue growth of 6.5% year-over-year. We were pleased to report another quarter of record consumer deposits and launch major initiatives to expand our reach in the small business segment as we onboarded a strategic small business credit card relationship, launched Business Essentials, an innovative suite of new products, and established new banker teams in expansion markets.
These results reflect strong execution against our strategic priorities and better interconnectivity across our organization. We remain focused on bringing innovative solutions to our clients, investing in our business, creating a culture of high-performance and delivering exceptional long-term value for our shareholders. On behalf of all of us at U.S. Bank, I want to thank our clients and shareholders for their continued trust and partnership.”
— Gunjan Kedia, Chairman and CEO, U.S. Bancorp
Business and Other Highlights
U.S. Bank launches USBDC Stablecoin
U.S. Bank has successfully completed a live pilot transaction using USBDC, its proprietary U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin, for a cross-border payment between U.S. Bank entities in North America and Europe, demonstrating the potential for 24/7 transactions. Conducted on the Stellar blockchain, the pilot showed the bank can move value on-chain while maintaining integration with its existing finance, risk, compliance and operations infrastructure. The transaction also validated U.S. Bank’s internally developed Digital Asset Platform and evaluated key capabilities, including minting, payment redemption, freezing and clawbacks, managing and moving tokenized assets, and creating a foundation for issuing. Looking ahead, U.S. Bank is exploring applications including liquidity management, collateral mobility and cross-border treasury operations, with the initiative representing another step in its broader digital asset strategy to use blockchain technology to improve efficiency, transparency and settlement speed while maintaining the safety, security and reliability expected by clients.
U.S. Bank launches new credit cards for small businesses
U.S. Bank has launched two new small-business credit cards, Business Essentials and Business Essentials Plus, offering unlimited 2% cash back on eligible purchases and additional rewards for customers with qualifying business checking balances. Business Essentials has no annual fee and can earn up to 2.5% total cash back, while the $295-annual-fee Plus card can earn up to 3.5% and automatically provides 5% cash back on the cardholder’s top spending category, subject to an annual limit. Both cards include tools designed to simplify expense management, including Spend Management and ExtendPay, while new cardholders can qualify for cash-back welcome offers of $500 or $1,000, depending on the card. U.S. Bank is supporting the launch with a new advertising campaign featuring entrepreneur and actress Jessica Alba as the spokesperson for both cards, emphasizing its broader strategy of building deeper relationships with small-business owners through integrated banking, payments and expense-management solutions.

Investor contact: Brian Mauney, Brian.Mauney@usbank.com | Media contact: Jeff Shelman, Jeffrey.Shelman@usbank.com

Net income attributable to U.S. Bancorp was $2,202 million for the third quarter of 2026, $201 million higher than the third quarter of 2025 and $25 million higher than the second quarter of 2026. Diluted earnings per common share was $1.34 in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $1.22 in the third quarter of 2025 and $1.35 in the second quarter of 2026.
The year-over-year increase in net income attributable to U.S. Bancorp was driven by higher total net revenue, partially offset by higher noninterest expense and higher provision for credit losses. Net interest income increased 5.6 percent on a taxable-equivalent basis, primarily due to loan growth, the impact of the small business credit card portfolio purchase and benefits from fixed asset repricing, while net interest margin increased to 2.84 percent from 2.75 percent. Noninterest income increased 13.1 percent, reflecting higher capital markets revenue including the impact of the BTIG acquisition, higher trust and investment management fees, and higher corporate payment and treasury management revenue. Noninterest expense increased 7.1 percent primarily due to the impact of the BTIG acquisition, as well as higher compensation and employee benefits expense, higher technology and communications expense, and increased marketing and business development expense. The provision for credit losses increased 14.5 percent, reflecting the impact of the small business credit card portfolio purchase, partially offset by improvement in the economic outlook and favorable credit performance.
Compared with the second quarter of 2026, net income attributable to U.S. Bancorp increased primarily due to higher total net revenue, partially offset by higher noninterest expense and higher provision for credit losses. Net interest income increased 2.3 percent on a taxable-equivalent basis, primarily driven by benefits from the small business credit card portfolio purchase, fixed asset repricing and the impact of higher interest rates, while net interest margin increased to 2.84 percent from 2.79 percent. Noninterest income increased 4.7 percent, reflecting higher capital markets revenue due to the BTIG acquisition, higher trust and investment management fees and higher corporate payment and treasury management revenue, partially offset by lower merchant processing services revenue. Noninterest expense increased 1.5 percent, reflecting higher compensation and employee benefits expense primarily due to a full quarter of BTIG expenses in the third quarter, along with higher technology and communications expense, partially offset by a decrease in other noninterest expense. The provision for credit losses increased 21.6 percent, reflecting the impact of the small business credit card portfolio purchase, partially offset by improvement in the economic outlook and favorable credit performance.

Net interest income on a taxable-equivalent basis was $4,490 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $239 million (5.6 percent) compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase primarily reflected loan growth, the impact of the small business credit card portfolio purchase and benefits from fixed asset repricing. Average earning assets were $13.3 billion (2.1 percent) higher than the third quarter of 2025, reflecting an increase of $30.4 billion (8.0 percent) in average loans, partially offset by a decrease of $12.8 billion (26.7 percent) in average interest-bearing deposits with banks and a decrease of $7.1 billion (4.1 percent) in average investment securities, reflecting tactical balance sheet management actions.
On a linked quarter basis, net interest income on a taxable-equivalent basis increased $103 million (2.3 percent) primarily driven by benefits from the small business credit card portfolio purchase, fixed asset repricing and the impact of higher interest rates. Average earning assets were $1.8 billion (0.3 percent) higher than the prior quarter, reflecting increases of $4.1 billion (1.0 percent) in average loans and $2.6 billion (8.0 percent) in average interest-bearing deposits with banks, partially offset by a decrease of $4.2 billion (2.5 percent) in average investment securities.
Net interest margin was 2.84 percent in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 2.75 percent in the third quarter of 2025 and 2.79 percent in the second quarter of 2026. The increase from the prior year reflected benefits from fixed asset repricing and improved asset mix. The increase from the linked quarter was driven by the benefits from fixed asset repricing along with impacts of the small business credit card portfolio purchase.

Average total loans for the third quarter of 2026 increased $30.4 billion (8.0 percent) compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase was driven by growth in total commercial loans, commercial real estate loans and credit card loans. Growth in total commercial loans reflected higher corporate loans and loans to financial institutions. Growth in total commercial real estate loans was primarily driven by commercial mortgage originations, while credit card loan growth reflected the purchase of a small business credit card portfolio in the third quarter of 2026, along with higher sales volumes.
Compared with the second quarter of 2026, average total loans increased $4.1 billion (1.0 percent), driven by growth in credit card loans, commercial real estate loans and other retail loans. Growth in credit card loans included the impact of the small business credit card portfolio purchase, while commercial real estate loan growth was primarily due to commercial mortgage originations. Growth in other retail loans was primarily driven by higher retail leasing balances.

Average total deposits in the third quarter of 2026 increased $14.8 billion (2.9 percent) compared with the third quarter of 2025. Average total interest-bearing deposits increased, driven by growth in Consumer and Business Banking savings accounts and Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking money market accounts, partially offset by lower time deposit balances in Treasury and Corporate Support. Time deposit balances are managed as an alternative funding source based on relative pricing and liquidity considerations.
Compared with the second quarter of 2026, average total deposits increased $11.5 billion (2.2 percent), driven by growth in Consumer and Business Banking savings accounts and Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking money market accounts.

Third quarter noninterest income of $3,480 million increased $402 million (13.1 percent) compared with the third quarter of 2025, driven by higher capital markets revenue, trust and investment management fees, corporate payment and treasury management revenue and other revenue. Capital markets revenue increased primarily due to the contribution from BTIG, along with higher syndication and client-related derivative activity. Trust and investment management fees increased due to business growth and favorable market conditions. Corporate payment and treasury management revenue increased due to higher sales, while other revenue increased due to higher equity investment gains.
Compared with the second quarter of 2026, noninterest income increased $155 million (4.7 percent), driven by higher capital markets revenue, trust and investment management fees, corporate payment and treasury management revenue and other revenue, partially offset by lower merchant processing services revenue. Capital markets revenue increased primarily due to a full quarter of contribution from BTIG. Trust and investment management fees increased due to business growth. Corporate payment and treasury management revenue increased due to higher sales, while other revenue increased due to higher equity investment gains. Merchant processing services decreased due to seasonality.

Third quarter noninterest expense was $4,493 million, an increase of $296 million (7.1 percent) compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase reflected the impact of the BTIG acquisition, higher compensation and employee benefits expense primarily due to merit increases, higher technology and communications expense related to investments in product and technology development, and increased marketing and business development initiatives, partially offset by lower other expense.
Compared with the second quarter of 2026, noninterest expense increased $65 million (1.5 percent). The increase reflected higher compensation and employee benefits expense primarily due to a full quarter of BTIG expenses in the third quarter, and higher technology and communications expense related to investments in product and technology development, partially offset by lower other expense.
Provision for Income Taxes
The provision for income taxes for the third quarter of 2026 resulted in a tax rate of 21.8 percent on a taxable-equivalent basis (effective tax rate of 21.2 percent), compared with 21.6 percent on a taxable-equivalent basis (effective tax rate of 20.7 percent) in the third quarter of 2025, and 20.5 percent on a taxable-equivalent basis (effective tax rate of 19.7 percent) in the second quarter of 2026.

8
U.S. Bancorp Third Quarter 2026 Results
The provision for credit losses was $654 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $538 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $571 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase on a year-over-year basis was primarily driven by the impact of recording the initial provision for credit losses of $135 million related to the purchase of a small business credit card portfolio in the third quarter of 2026, partially offset by improvement in the economic outlook and favorable credit performance. The increase on a linked quarter basis was primarily driven by the impact of the small business credit card portfolio purchase, partially offset by improvement in the economic outlook and favorable credit performance. While economic conditions have shown improvement, the Company continues to monitor economic uncertainty related to interest rates, inflationary pressures, including those related to evolving geopolitical events, as well as other economic factors that may affect the financial strength of corporate and consumer borrowers.
Total net charge-offs were $523 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $536 million in both the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025. The net charge-off ratio in the third quarter of 2026 was 0.51 percent, compared with 0.53 percent in the second quarter of 2026 and 0.56 percent in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in net charge-offs on a linked quarter basis was driven by lower net charge-offs on credit card loans, partially offset by higher net charge-offs on commercial real estate loans. Compared with the prior year quarter, lower net charge-offs on commercial real estate loans and credit card loans were partially offset by higher net charge-offs on commercial loans.
The allowance for credit losses was $8,165 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $7,979 million at June 30, 2026, and $7,897 million at September 30, 2025. The increase in the allowance for credit losses compared with the linked quarter and prior year quarter was primarily due to the impacts of recording the initial provision for credit losses of $135 million and initial allowance for acquired credit losses of $55 million related to the purchase of the small business credit card portfolio, partially offset by improving credit quality and economic outlook. The allowance for credit losses represented 1.97 percent of period-end loans at September 30, 2026, and 636 percent of nonperforming loans at September 30, 2026.
Nonperforming assets were $1,324 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $1,346 million at June 30, 2026, and $1,654 million at September 30, 2025. The decrease from the prior year quarter primarily reflected the resolution of commercial and commercial mortgage nonperforming loans. The ratio of nonperforming assets to loans and other real estate was 0.32 percent at September 30, 2026. Accruing loans 90 days or more past due were $743 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $735 million at June 30, 2026, and $840 million at September 30, 2025. The decrease in accruing loans 90 days or more past due from the prior year quarter was primarily due to the resolution of elevated prior year residential mortgage delinquencies.

Total U.S. Bancorp shareholders’ equity was $66.4 billion at September 30, 2026, compared with $67.4 billion at June 30, 2026, and $63.3 billion at September 30, 2025. The increase from the prior year quarter reflected the impacts of corporate earnings and the common shares issued as consideration for the acquisition of BTIG, partially offset by dividends paid.
All regulatory capital ratios continue to be in excess of “well-capitalized” requirements. The common equity tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets ratio using the Basel III standardized approach was 10.8 percent at both September 30, 2026, and June 30, 2026, compared with 10.9 percent at September 30, 2025.

About U.S. Bancorp
Headquartered in Minneapolis, U.S. Bancorp is the parent company of U.S. Bank National Association, the fifth-largest commercial bank in the United States. The company's three major business lines serve 15 million clients globally, and its team of nearly 70,000 people invest their hearts and minds to power human potential every day. Ranked 110th on the Fortune 500, U.S. Bancorp is deeply respected for its culture and long-term stewardship and admired for its diversified business mix and product capabilities.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures
In addition to capital ratios defined by banking regulators, the Company considers various other measures when evaluating capital utilization and adequacy, including: 
•Tangible common equity to tangible assets,
•Tangible common equity to risk-weighted assets,
•Tangible book value per common share, and
•Return on tangible common equity.
These capital measures are viewed by management as useful additional methods of evaluating the Company’s utilization of its capital held and the level of capital available to withstand unexpected negative market or economic conditions. Additionally, presentation of these measures allows investors, analysts and banking regulators to assess the Company’s capital position and use of capital relative to other financial services companies. These capital measures are not defined in generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) or in banking regulations. Management believes this information helps investors assess trends in the Company’s capital utilization and adequacy.
The Company also discloses net interest income and related ratios and analysis on a taxable-equivalent basis, which may also be considered non-GAAP financial measures. The Company believes this presentation to be the preferred industry measurement of net interest income as it provides a relevant comparison of net interest income arising from taxable and tax-exempt sources. In addition, certain performance measures utilize net interest income on a taxable-equivalent basis, including the efficiency ratio, operating leverage, net interest margin, and tax rate.
There may be limits in the usefulness of these measures to investors. As a result, the Company encourages readers to consider the consolidated financial statements and other financial information contained in this press release in their entirety, and not to rely on any single financial measure. A table follows that shows the Company’s calculation of these non-GAAP financial measures.

Business Segments
The Company’s major business segments are Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking, Consumer and Business Banking, Payment Services, and Treasury and Corporate Support. Business segment results are derived from the Company’s business unit profitability reporting systems by specifically attributing managed balance sheet assets, deposits and other liabilities and their related income or expense. Designations, assignments and allocations change from time to time as management systems are enhanced, methods of evaluating performance or product lines change or business segments are realigned to better respond to the Company’s diverse customer base. During 2026, certain organization and methodology changes were made, including moving the Impact Finance business unit from the Treasury and Corporate Support business segment to the Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking business segment. In addition, card revenue generated from debit cards, which was previously included in the Payment Services business segment, is now included in the Consumer and Business Banking business segment. Prior period results were recast and presented on a comparable basis.

Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking provides core banking, specialized lending, transaction and payment processing, capital markets, asset management, and brokerage and investment related services to wealth, middle market, large corporate, commercial real estate, government and institutional clients, and also includes investments in tax-advantaged projects.
Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking generated $2,243 million of income before provision and taxes in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $1,838 million in the third quarter of 2025, and contributed $1,598 million of the Company’s net income in the third quarter of 2026.
Total net revenue increased compared with the third quarter of 2025, driven by growth in net interest income from higher loan and deposit balances and growth in noninterest income, primarily due to higher capital markets revenue driven by the contribution from BTIG and higher syndication and client-related derivative activity, and higher trust and investment management fees due to business growth and favorable market conditions.
Noninterest expense increased compared with the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to higher compensation and employee benefits expense and higher technology and communications expense, both driven by the BTIG acquisition.
The provision for credit losses decreased compared with the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to favorable credit performance.

Consumer and Business Banking comprises consumer banking, small business banking, debit cards and consumer lending. Products and services are delivered through banking offices, telephone servicing and sales, online services, direct mail, ATMs, mobile devices, distributed mortgage loan officers, and intermediary relationships including auto dealerships, mortgage banks, and strategic business partners.
Consumer and Business Banking generated $916 million of income before provision and taxes in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $853 million in the third quarter of 2025, and contributed $633 million of the Company’s net income in the third quarter of 2026.
Total net revenue decreased slightly compared with the third quarter of 2025 due to lower noninterest income, partially offset by higher net interest income. Net interest income increased primarily due to higher deposit balances, while noninterest income decreased primarily due to lower mortgage banking revenue, reflecting lower gain on sale activity.
Noninterest expense decreased compared with the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to lower net shared services expense.
The provision for credit losses increased compared with the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to growth in commercial and other retail loans.

Payment Services includes consumer and business credit cards, stored-value cards, corporate, government and purchasing card services and merchant processing.
Payment Services generated $828 million of income before provision and taxes in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $749 million in the third quarter of 2025, and contributed $175 million of the Company’s net income in the third quarter of 2026.
Total net revenue increased compared with the third quarter of 2025, driven by an increase in net interest income, primarily due to higher loan balances including the impact of the small business credit card portfolio purchase, and an increase in noninterest income, primarily due to higher corporate payment and treasury management revenue and higher card revenue, both driven by higher sales volume.
Noninterest expense increased primarily due to higher technology and communications expense, higher compensation and employee benefits expense and higher marketing and business development expense.
The provision for credit losses increased compared with the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to the impact of recording the initial provision for credit losses related to the purchase of the small business credit card portfolio.

Treasury and Corporate Support includes the Company’s investment portfolios, funding, capital management, interest rate risk management, income taxes not allocated to the business segments, and the residual aggregate of those expenses associated with corporate activities that are managed on a consolidated basis.
Treasury and Corporate Support generated a $510 million loss before provision and taxes in the third quarter of 2026, compared with a $308 million loss before provision and taxes in the third quarter of 2025, and recorded a net loss of $204 million in the third quarter of 2026.
Total net revenue decreased compared with the third quarter of 2025, driven by lower net interest income, primarily due to lower interest-bearing deposits with banks and investment securities balances, partially offset by lower funding costs and benefits from fixed asset repricing, as well as lower noninterest income driven by losses on the sales of investment securities.
Noninterest expense increased compared with the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to higher technology and communications expense, net shared services expense, and compensation and employee benefits expense.
The provision for credit losses decreased compared with the third quarter of 2025 primarily due to improvement in the economic outlook.
Income taxes are assessed to each business segment at a managerial tax rate of 25.0 percent with the residual tax expense or benefit to arrive at the consolidated effective tax rate included in Treasury and Corporate Support.
